title: Ang 1102–1105: Kabir in Maru
tomorrow: who but You would put a crown on someone the world shunned?

cards: Warrior shows up all over: a warrior pose in yoga class, warrior mode on a gym shirt, a game where you level up your warrior. So here's the puzzle.
This whole stretch of the Granth has been humble walks, cupped hands and answers of peace. Then, on ang 1105, the saint Kabir suddenly sounds like a war drum.
The drum beats in the sky, he says, and the warrior has taken the field. Why would a book this full of peace stop to praise a fighter?

teach.b: From ang 1102, Kabir's hymns in Maru. Kabir isn't one of the Gurus. He's one of the Bhagats, saints whose hymns the Gurus gathered into the Granth beside their own.

teach.h: THE DRUM BEATS IN THE SKY.
teach.b: Here's his salok, in paraphrase: the drum beats in the sky, the blow lands on the target; the warrior has taken the field, now is the time to fight.

Then the key line: know him as a true warrior who fights for the sake of the deen, and who, even if it costs him piece by piece, never leaves the field. That's the solution to the puzzle. Look at who the fight is for.
The word deen is read two ways. Some readers hear faith, the right path; others hear the poor, the helpless, the ones with no one in their corner.

Either way, the warrior Kabir praises isn't fighting for glory or for himself. He's fighting for something beyond himself, and he doesn't quit when it gets expensive. So the book of peace hasn't changed its mind.
The humble walk and the true warrior are one person on two different days: calm when mocked, and immovable when someone weaker needs a stand.
Some readers hear an inner battle, too: against ego, against the pull to walk away. The true warrior.

how: Kabir's Maru salok of the true warrior (soora) is sung in kirtan and often quoted in Sikh teaching about courage on behalf of others.

games.q: a quiet classmate is getting piled on in a group chat, and it keeps going for days. what would Kabir's true warrior do?
o: stand up for her, and keep standing even when it gets costly.
roast the bullies harder, so everyone sees who wins.
stay out of it; peace means never getting involved.
games.why: the true warrior fights for the deen and never leaves the field: for someone beyond himself, and steadily.

practice: Think of one person who could use someone in their corner right now. Name the thing most likely to make you step back from that, being busy, being awkward, being scared.
Then picture one small, specific way you'd hold your ground anyway.
